prompt: Products with a missing category_id still name their category in category_raw. For each of them, which parent category does category_raw point to? These tables may hold errors. A category_raw value names a child category when it equals that category's category_name, ignoring letter case and spaces at the start or end, and points to that child's parent_category. It names the parent TV & Video itself when it is 'tv & video', 'tv en video', 'tv/video' or 'téléviseurs', ignoring letter case and outer spaces. Return two columns, in this order: product_id and parent_category, missing when category_raw names neither. Return one row for each product with a missing category_id. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the CASE that turns category_raw into a parent category.
Spot the parent's own spellings first, then fall back to the parent of the category whose name matches; a LEFT JOIN keeps a value that matches nothing.
why_this_works: The CASE spots the parent's own spellings after cleaning, and the LEFT JOIN on the cleaned name finds the parent of a child category.
